13.text: Exposure is, on the whole, prevalent among the Chukchee, and must be

14.text: considered as their fundamental method of funeral. The Koryak living

15.text: more to the south, where there is an abundance of fuel, have, on the con-

16.text: trary, adopted exclusively cremation of bodies. The Keˊrek, in whose

17.text: country, again, there is a dearth of fuel, throw their dead into the sea from

18.text: some steep rock on the shore.

19.text: After the method of disposing of the body has been decided, the deceased

20.text: person is asked about the place he chooses for the funeral. Hill-slopes, and,

21.text: in general, all higher places well dried in summer by the sun, are considered

22.text: fittest for the purpose. Several of these are mentioned aloud before the dead

23.text: body, till the sudden feeling of lessened weight makes the performer move the

24.text: staff upward, which, as explained before,² renders the answer affirmative. Then

25.text: the method of the last journey is chosen. Every man who has reindeer will, of

26.text: course, “desire” to use them for his funeral journey, because it is necessarily

27.text: very long and tiresome. But a very poor man, who has no reindeer of his own,

28.text: has to perform this journey on foot. The reindeer of another man — newly

29.text: bought, or borrowed for the purpose — are of no use in these circumstances.

30.text: The approaches to the country of the dead are very intricate; and while

31.text: the new-comer wanders about, seeking the abode of his own family, the former

32.text: owners of the reindeer will recognize them, even from afar, by their smell,

33.text: and will immediately intercept the wanderer in order to take from him their

34.text: belongings. The same apprehension is felt respecting newly borrowed clothing

35.text: or skins. Therefore a man who dies suddenly in a strange country — for

36.text: instance, on a trading-expedition — must be taken to the funeral place in

37.text: his ordinary clothing, even though there are people around who would lend

38.text: him a new suit. In a former work³ I have given a description, taken down

39.text: from a native, of such a funeral in a strange country. The deceased had
